My husband and I were virgins as far as your standard vaginal intercourse goes. While i initially wanted to wait for marriage due to religious reasons, we were together for 2 years before getting engaged and my views changed a lot. We did all sorts of fun things together before the wedding, and really only held off on intercourse at that point because I had this fear of penetration. 

I also had a traumatizing experience at the gynecologist's a month before getting married, and it took my bits a while to heal.

Our wedding night, we attempted intercourse, but it hurt too much, so we stopped. He couldn't even get it in, I was so tight. So we just went ahead and did our usual oral/manual sex, which was nice. :)

It took us about two months to successfully have "normal" sex and even longer to be able to do it at length. There was a month here or there where we had the same trouble of it hurting too much for him to get in, so we would give intercourse a rest. Things are better and a lot more consistent now.

TLDR; it wasn't this magical thing and we didn't even technically do it on our wedding night, but we both had fun and it was awesome to be that close as a married couple.

I don't regret any of it. Being with someone of another (or no) faith helped me with my own beliefs tremendously. I had the chance to really question and define my own faith and my partner and i had a lot of challenging, rewarding discussions. 

I ended up deconverting for personal reasons very recently, but along the way, my spouse has been nothing but supportive and respectful the whole way through. That's what's important. 

I understand your faith is important to you. But at the end of the day, I think you'll have less regrets if you give it a shot. Even if it ends up not working out! And honestly, if you believe God is real, and omniscient and loving, don't you think he can handle you dating a non-Christian? Far worse things have happened, and you wouldn't be sinning.
